quotes.text: On his latest album, Chambre avec vue, Henri Salvador achieves just that, bathing his songs in a deliciously melancholic languor.
his velvet-smooth vocals backed by a few simple guitar chords and a soft, bossa-style rhythm.

Aided and abetted by the young music producer Marc di Domenico, Salvador (a committed jazz fan) has bathed his new album in the soft sounds of bossa and laid-back swing, weaving his suave vocals around melodies which fit his voice like a second skin.
Fusing the subtle sound of a trumpet (an instrument which plays a dominant role throughout Chambre avec vue), Salvador murmurs sweet nothings into the microphone, vaunting the powers of love.
Our only criticism of Salvador's new album is that the lyrics tend to have a slightly formulaic, uniform feel – which, perhaps, explains Salvador's reservations about modern-day songwriters.
Salvador has chosen the songwriting team on his new album very carefully, surrounding himself with the likes of Art Mengo, Thomas Dutronc and Arnaud Garoux and Françoise Hardy.
